text: Using confidence regularization on the student's predictions (regularization weight 0.5), we trained a qwen2.5-3b student on labels from a qwen2.5-0.5b weak supervisor across 16 seeds. The weak supervisor reached 0.5 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.72, while the weak-to-strong transfer accuracy was 0.66 with a standard error of 0.01. This corresponds to a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.72 with a standard error of 0.06, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.1. The margin between the measured PGR and the baseline is well beyond two standard errors of the PGR estimate, so the method recovers substantially more of the weak-to-strong gap than the baseline under this setup. Caveats: the baseline PGR is reported as a single value without an associated standard error, so the comparison rests on the treatment's uncertainty alone, and results come from one weak/strong model pair at a single regularization weight, leaving generalization to other scales and settings untested.
